statements.statement: New revenue available for appropriation beyond last year, across all town and school departments, is estimated at just over this figure.
Monty Tech's assessment is about this share of the total operating budget, implying roughly this much additional appropriation needed for FY27.
After assuming a health insurance increase, only about this amount of the new revenue estimate would remain for all other town and school cost increases combined.
The revenue estimate assumes level state aid; the actual figure is not yet known.
Health insurance is expected to rise by about this percentage, with the confirmed figure not available until after the insurance trust's announcement later in January.
It appears the schools will seek to pursue a Proposition 2½ override for FY27.
The fire chief has indicated a need for a fourth shift, which may also factor into an override request alongside school and general town needs.

warnings.condition: if the budget is balanced without a Proposition 2½ override
warnings.prediction: Balancing the budget without an override would mean real, significant staffing and service cuts, not minor items.
The town manager said she will be shocked or astonished if the town can keep to the current budget-season meeting schedule given staffing shortages in the finance office.

warnings.condition: if GLP-1 coverage is removed from the plan
warnings.prediction: If GLP-1 medication coverage is dropped by the insurance plan, the town manager does not expect the health insurance rate increase to still come in near 20% with a new justification offered instead.

warnings.about: staff morale and retention amid budget-cut discussions
warnings.prediction: Talk of budget cuts risks creating a fear factor among town employees that could cause them to leave their jobs.

warnings.about: support for a future Proposition 2½ override
warnings.condition: unless the town first pursues cost savings and budget restructuring
warnings.prediction: A member said he will not support another operational override until the town does the hard work of reviewing and restructuring the budget first.
